title: DigitalOwl Reviews
summary: DigitalOwl reviews, covering its AI medical record analysis, Self-Serve legal plans, the Datavant acquisition and ChartSwap Insights transition, plus how Codes Health pairs retrieval with plaintiff-focused analysis on a flat fee.
body_markdown:
For plaintiff law firms handling personal injury, mass tort, and medical malpractice cases, the medical record analysis platform you pick shapes case timelines, staff workload, and litigation outcomes. DigitalOwl built its reputation in the insurance sector and now markets to legal teams as well. So how does it fit a plaintiff practice? This review covers DigitalOwl's capabilities, pricing, and the questions worth asking during the Datavant transition, and looks at why some firms focused on[plaintiff litigation](https://www.getcodeshealth.com/) want a different workflow shape.


## **Key Takeaways**


-


DigitalOwl has deep roots in insurance underwriting and claims and now markets its platform to both insurance and legal professionals, including personal injury, mass tort, and medical malpractice workflows


-


The platform advertises analysis of thousands of pages in an hour or less, with 97% or higher accuracy overall and Self-Serve third-party tested at over 98%


-


Datavant completed its acquisition of DigitalOwl on October 8, 2025, and DigitalOwl is becoming ChartSwap Insights


-


Datavant already offers record retrieval with optional AI-powered analysis through ChartSwap Insights, while a more fully unified DigitalOwl Self-Serve experience is still rolling out


-


Self-Serve legal plans start at $99 per month, and DigitalOwl markets Self-Serve to firms processing under 30,000 pages monthly


-


Codes Health works toward complete records in a couple of weeks with retrieval, AI analysis, and human verification in one flat-fee workflow


-


Incomplete authorizations are a leading cause of denied requests, and pre-submission AI validation catches them before a resubmission is needed


## **What is DigitalOwl?**


DigitalOwl is an AI-powered medical record analysis platform founded around 2018, with offices in Israel and New York. Its co-founder has written that the company started in 2018, though some third-party listings show 2017.


The company's core technology grew up serving insurance carriers handling life insurance underwriting, property and casualty claims, and risk assessment. DigitalOwl publicly identifies relationships with organizations including RGA, Nationwide, AAA Life, and Legal & General America, which speak to its strength in insurance-focused medical analysis where speed and risk identification drive underwriting decisions.


In September 2025, Datavant announced an agreement to acquire DigitalOwl, and the deal closed on October 8, 2025. Datavant did not publicly disclose the purchase price; CTech estimated the transaction at more than $200 million. The combination pairs DigitalOwl's AI analysis with Datavant's retrieval infrastructure, and DigitalOwl is transitioning to the ChartSwap Insights brand.


## **DigitalOwl's Core Features and Capabilities**


### **AI-Powered Medical Summaries**


DigitalOwl processes records through its AI engine to generate:


-


Medical chronologies organizing patient encounters by date


-


Document summaries condensing records into key findings


-


De-duplication to cut page review burden


-


Click-to-evidence sourcing linking summaries back to original documents


DigitalOwl currently advertises 97% or higher accuracy overall and says its Self-Serve legal platform has been third-party tested at over 98% accuracy. The public marketing materials reviewed for this article don't provide the full testing methodology, sample size, or error definitions behind those figures, so firms should request that documentation during evaluation.


### **Processing Speed**


For records already in hand, DigitalOwl states it can process thousands of pages in an hour or less. That speed suits workflows where a reviewer needs a rapid read on existing documentation.


### **Self-Serve Portal**


DigitalOwl markets Self-Serve for Legal to firms processing fewer than 30,000 pages per month, with 24/7 access and a 7-day free trial. The autonomous access model appeals to tech-forward smaller teams that would rather process on demand than coordinate with a vendor.


### **Enterprise Integration**


The Connect product provides API access to structured medical data for organizations integrating analysis into existing systems. Enterprise prospects are directed to contact DigitalOwl for pricing and deployment details.


## **DigitalOwl in Insurance and Legal Markets**


DigitalOwl's longest-standing market position is insurance underwriting, where its technology has earned recognition including the 2025 Natural Language Generation Platform of the Year for Medical Record Reviews and a 2025 Product of the Year award. Its newsroom also highlights a 2026 BIG Innovation Award for Self-Serve.


Insurance customers publish favorable feedback on DigitalOwl's site. Executives at Simplicity Group, Baltimore Life, and Nationwide describe long-running working relationships, faster attending physician statement review, and an interface underwriters adopted readily. Plaintiff law firm testimonials are less prominent in DigitalOwl's public materials.


On the legal side, DigitalOwl's current positioning is broader than its insurance origins suggest. Its legal pages market functionality for personal injury, mass tort, and medical malpractice, describe examining records for evidence of negligence, and say the AI interprets medical records through the lens of causation, damages, and liability. Demand package creation and analysis are also advertised.


## **DigitalOwl for Legal Teams: Strengths and Considerations**


### **Where DigitalOwl Excels**


For legal teams that already have efficient record retrieval running, DigitalOwl provides:


-


Fast analysis of records already obtained


-


Strong de-duplication reducing review burden


-


Established enterprise infrastructure, with DigitalOwl stating that its platform adheres to SOC 2 Type II and HIPAA requirements and representing Self-Serve as GDPR compliant


-


Self-serve access for smaller operations


Firms handling insurance defense alongside plaintiff work may find the insurance depth useful for certain case types.


### **What to Confirm During Evaluation**


A few areas are worth asking about directly rather than inferring from marketing pages.


-


**Specific feature depth:** DigitalOwl advertises negligence-focused analysis, though the public materials reviewed here don't name a feature specifically called breach-of-care detection. It advertises damages and cost-related analysis, but those materials don't identify a dedicated future medical expense extraction feature. Firms that rely on those specific outputs should ask how each is implemented.


-


**Retrieval workflow shape:** Datavant is actively combining DigitalOwl's analysis technology with its retrieval products under ChartSwap Insights, and already offers retrieval with optional AI-powered summary and analysis through its Smart Request workflow. At the same time, DigitalOwl's own Self-Serve page still describes a next-generation unified retrieval-and-analysis experience as coming. Worth[confirming what is available](https://www.getcodeshealth.com/blogs/digitalowl-alternatives) today versus what remains on the roadmap.


-


**Transition timing:** The rebrand to ChartSwap Insights is underway. Product direction, support structure, and contract terms during a transition are reasonable things to pin down before signing.


## **Retrieval and Analysis: How the Workflow Fits Together**


One of the bigger structural questions for plaintiff firms is whether to run separate vendors for retrieval and analysis or work with one platform that does both.


### **The Multi-Vendor Challenge**


Firms running analysis in one place and retrieval in another deal with:


-


Multiple vendor relationships requiring separate contracts, contacts, and billing


-


Coordination overhead as staff track which records have been retrieved versus analyzed


-


Extended timelines as records move between systems


-


Additional administrative cost from managing parallel relationships


### **Integrated Workflow Advantages**


Combining retrieval and analysis can reduce handoffs and vendor coordination, which may shorten workflows and cut administrative burden. It's a structural argument rather than a measured one, and the size of the benefit depends on how much coordination your team is doing today.


[Codes Health](https://www.getcodeshealth.com/) takes this integrated approach, handling retrieval through clearinghouse connections, provider portals, fax, email, and phone outreach, then applying AI analysis to the complete record set with human verification before delivery. It works toward complete records in a couple of weeks.


On speed claims generally, Codes Health notes that services advertising same-day retrieval typically return only the records already available electronically, which leaves the firm or the client chasing the rest, an experience it says contributes to client churn. Codes Health does not market same-day delivery.


## **Pricing and Cost Structure**


### **DigitalOwl Pricing**


DigitalOwl offers multiple Self-Serve plans starting at $99 per month, with additional features and deeper analysis available on higher plans. It markets Self-Serve to firms processing under 30,000 pages monthly. Enterprise pricing is handled through direct contact with the company.


### **Cost Considerations for Contingency Practices**


A few things worth clarifying with any subscription-based platform:


-


Plan fit as caseload volume fluctuates month to month


-


What each tier includes, since deeper analysis may sit on a higher plan


-


Separate retrieval costs, if another vendor handles record acquisition


-


Contract terms during the ChartSwap Insights transition


### **Alternative Pricing Models**


Flat-fee pricing avoids subscription tier math entirely. That approach can suit contingency-fee firm economics, where cash flow predictability matters more than optimizing a monthly plan.


## **How Codes Health Compares**


For plaintiff firms wanting a platform[built around litigation workflows](https://www.getcodeshealth.com/blogs/digitalowl-alternatives) , Codes Health approaches the problem from a different starting point.


### **Key Differentiators**


**Integrated workflow:**[Codes Health](https://www.getcodeshealth.com/) combines retrieval and analysis in a single platform. Complete records arrive with AI analysis and human verification included, which removes the coordination work of running separate vendor relationships.


**Plaintiff-focused AI outputs:** the platform advertises specific extractions built for litigation:


-


Breach-in-care identification for medical malpractice work


-


Future medical expense extraction for damages documentation


-


Pre-existing condition flagging and other hidden case facts


-


Case-context analysis that helps surface causation evidence


**Purpose-built, not general-purpose:** general AI platforms like ChatGPT are not designed for litigation-grade medical record review. They don't retrieve records, validate authorizations, follow up with providers, or verify completeness. Codes Health's platform is built for this work and analyzes medical records with high precision for legal teams, with AI insights verified by humans.


**Authorization quality review:** AI validation catches incomplete authorizations, a leading cause of denied requests, before submission. Missing signatures, misspellings, unclear expiration dates, and missing dates of service get flagged before they cost you a resubmission.


**Filevine integration:** The Filevine partnership lets legal teams initiate requests, track progress, and receive completed records without leaving their case management environment. For high-volume customers, Codes Health also builds custom integrations with CRM platforms and other medical software systems.


**Flat-fee pricing:** pricing is structured as a flat fee rather than a volume-based subscription.


Codes Health's MIT-educated engineering team keeps building out additional workflows and products, so the platform continues to evolve, improve, and grow more comprehensive as the demands of modern legal practices change.


### **Reported Outcomes**


Codes Health reports customer outcomes including up to[80% less manual review](https://www.getcodeshealth.com/blogs/digitalowl-alternatives) , 50% more case capacity without additional staff, and, in some reported cases, 1.7x larger settlements.


These are company-reported customer outcomes rather than independently validated findings, and they should not be read as guaranteed results. Individual results vary based on case mix, firm size, and existing processes.


## **Choosing the Right Analysis Partner for Your Practice**


**Choose DigitalOwl when:**


-


You already have fast, reliable record retrieval running


-


Your practice includes insurance defense or carrier work


-


You need 24/7 self-serve access for a smaller team


-


Your monthly page volume fits comfortably in a Self-Serve plan


-


You prioritize analysis speed on records you already hold


**Choose Codes Health when:**


-


You want[retrieval and analysis combined](https://www.getcodeshealth.com/blogs/digitalowl-vs-wisedocs-vs-codes-health) in one plaintiff-focused workflow today


-


Named breach-in-care and future expense extraction outputs are central to your cases


-


Human verification of AI insights before delivery is a requirement


-


Proactive missing record detection before trial is a priority


-


Flat-fee predictability matters more than optimizing a monthly plan


-


Embedded case management integration would cut context switching


### **Questions to Ask Any Vendor**


Ask about typical turnaround for complete records rather than just the electronic ones, how the vendor handles providers who don't respond, what the AI does and where it sits in the workflow, how completeness is verified before delivery, what the pricing model is and what extra fees to expect, which integrations are supported including custom builds, and whether you can talk to references from similar practices. During an ownership transition, add one more: what is contractually committed today versus described as coming.


## **The Bottom Line**


Most of what slows a plaintiff firm's medical records workflow is preventable. Authorization defects that could have been caught before submission force a correction and a resubmission. Records get analyzed in one system after being retrieved in another, and the handoff costs days. Gaps go unnoticed until trial prep. Rapid-turnaround promises deliver what was already available electronically and leave the rest outstanding.


DigitalOwl has earned its position through strong technology, verified carrier relationships, fast processing, and a legal product that now covers negligence review, causation, damages, liability, and demand packages across personal injury, mass tort, and medical malpractice. With Datavant's retrieval infrastructure behind it, the retrieval gap that once defined the comparison is closing.


The honest distinction now is workflow shape rather than capability absence.[Codes Health](https://www.getcodeshealth.com/) was built from the start around plaintiff firm workflows, combining retrieval and analysis in one place, advertising specific breach-in-care and future expense extraction, verifying AI insights with humans before delivery, pricing on a flat fee, and embedding into Filevine. If your firm is coordinating vendors, waiting on handoffs, or finding documentation gaps during trial prep, that shape is worth evaluating.


## **Frequently Asked Questions**


### **What happened to DigitalOwl after the Datavant acquisition?**


Datavant announced the agreement in September 2025 and completed the acquisition on October 8, 2025. DigitalOwl is becoming ChartSwap Insights, and its analysis technology is being combined with Datavant's retrieval products. Firms should confirm current product availability and contract terms directly, since parts of the combined experience are still rolling out.


### **Does DigitalOwl handle medical record retrieval?**


DigitalOwl historically focused on analysis of records already obtained. Following the acquisition, Datavant already offers record retrieval with optional AI-powered summary and analysis through ChartSwap Insights via its Smart Request workflow. Separately, DigitalOwl's own Self-Serve page still describes a next-generation unified retrieval-and-analysis experience as forthcoming, so it's worth clarifying which[workflow you get](https://www.getcodeshealth.com/blogs/digitalowl-vs-inquery-vs-codes-health) today.


### **How accurate is DigitalOwl's AI analysis?**


DigitalOwl advertises 97% or higher accuracy overall and says its Self-Serve legal platform was third-party tested at over 98% accuracy. The public materials reviewed here don't publish the underlying methodology, sample size, or error definitions, so request that documentation during evaluation.


### **What's the difference between DigitalOwl and Codes Health for plaintiff firms?**


Codes Health was built around integrated retrieval and analysis for plaintiff law firms, while DigitalOwl historically emphasized analysis and insurance and is now being integrated with Datavant's retrieval infrastructure. Both market to personal injury, mass tort, and medical malpractice teams.[Codes Health differentiates](https://www.getcodeshealth.com/blogs/llamalab-vs-digitalowl-vs-codes-health) through named breach-in-care and future expense extraction, human verification of AI insights, flat-fee pricing, and an embedded Filevine workflow.


### **Is DigitalOwl HIPAA compliant?**


DigitalOwl states that its platform adheres to SOC 2 Type II and HIPAA requirements, and has represented its Self-Serve solution as GDPR compliant. Compliance standards like these are essential for any platform handling protected health information in legal workflows.


### **Can I try DigitalOwl before committing?**


DigitalOwl currently offers a 7-day free trial for its Self-Serve legal product, which lets smaller teams evaluate the analysis capabilities on real case records before choosing a paid plan.
